newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SPIRITS PRODUCER SEMA'S 1Q PROFIT, SALES DOWN.
newsitem.headline: SPIRITS PRODUCER SEMA'S 1Q PROFIT, SALES DOWN.

text.p: Lithuanian spirits producer Sema said on Thursday that its net profit and sales for the first three months of this year fell compared to the same period last year.
The company's economy director Antanas Stoka told Reuters that its net profit for the first quarter of this year fell to 396,935 litas from 1.7 million litas last year.
He added that sales also dropped, falling to 8.6 million litas in the first three months of this year compared to 12.7 million litas for the same period last year.
Stoka said that profit and sales fell because Russia on December 31 of last year unexpectedly raised the bond on spirits transported across its territory.
"We couldn't export any of our products for the first three months of this year because the bond demanded by Russian customs is four times the price of the product," he said.
"Our first shipment to Kazakhstan this year was only sent this week," he said, adding that profits and sales would rise in the second quarter.
Sema makes strong spirits used by other alcohol producers.
The company exports 50 percent of its products.
Stoka also said that the company's shareholders' meeting on April 25 would decide on a proposed 18 million litas share issue.
Stoka said that the issue had caught the eye of a number of investors, including Williams de Broe.

The company, which is 27.16 percent state-owned, recently increased its share capital to 20.7 million litas from 15.9 million litas with funds from its own reserves. The increase was registered with the securities commission last week.
Sema is listed on the Vilnius bourse's A list and is considered to be a strong candidate for inclusion on the official list.
Trade in its shares was suspended on April 15 for up to three months while it boosts its share capital.
